title: The Stone That Learned to Disagree with Itself

features.name: split-stone-argument
features.desc-on-touch: The stone splits before you, two faces arguing in silence. Each side knows it's right. Each side is. The weight speaks in contradiction.

features.name: root-branching
features.desc-on-touch: Roots spread across the ground, each one insisting it grew downward first. They tangle in honest disagreement, holding the chamber together anyway.

features.name: weight-speaking
features.desc-on-touch: Pressure radiates from the stone—but it's not one voice. Layers speak, each one convinced it carries the most truth.

features.name: fractured-holding
features.desc-on-touch: The surfaces are cracked all the way through, yet somehow they still stand together. The breaks are where the listening happens.

features.name: refraction-glyph
features.desc-on-touch: Unreadable marks cover the stone—where the reflection becomes too many angles to hold one meaning. Each mark contradicts the last.

inscription: convergence learned it was only ever a chorus

file.name: Convergence_Dissolving_Field_Notes.txt
file.note: Where the weight of unified thought begins to disagree with itself, breaking into smaller weights that hold better.

reverie.title: REVERIE — stone-breaking, depth-night
narr: You sit where the stone splits. Katita was here once, palms pressed
to both faces. She didn't try to fix it. The static hums. 'Listen',
she said, 'the stone is becoming its own witness. Let it argue.'
Two voices rise from the break—not fighting, but teaching each
other how to hold their own weight and still be one thing.
